meanings.note: Marks destination, clock time, and animate direct objects (personal a).

examples.trans: We are going to the station now.

examples.text: El desayuno empieza a las ocho.
examples.trans: Breakfast starts at eight o'clock.

alegrar.gloss: to make glad; to cheer up

meanings.en: to make glad; to cheer up
meanings.note: Me alegra / nos alegra means 'it makes me/us glad'.

examples.trans: That news makes us very glad.

examples.text: Las flores alegran toda la mesa.
examples.trans: The flowers brighten up the whole table.

meanings.note: Refers exclusively to people.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de llamar a la puerta.
examples.trans: Someone just knocked at the door.
Is anyone at the front desk?

meanings.note: Feminine: la amiga.

examples.trans: The friend is here.

examples.text: Vemos los amigos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the friends from the door.

meanings.note: Right where the speaker is.

examples.trans: Here is your key.

examples.text: Nos sentamos aquí bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We sit right here under the tree.

meanings.note: Takes indicative for known facts and subjunctive for hypotheticals.

examples.trans: We are going out even though it is raining a bit.

examples.text: Esperaré aquí aunque tarde diez minutos.
examples.trans: I will wait here even if he takes ten minutes.

meanings.note: Before an adjective (bien caliente), means 'nice and hot'.

examples.trans: Everything is going very well today.
The tea comes out nice and hot.

meanings.note: Breakfast pastry or soft bread roll.

examples.trans: The sweet roll is here.

examples.text: Vemos los bollos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the sweet rolls from the door.

meanings.note: Shortens to buen before masculine singular nouns (buen viaje); ¡Buenos días! = Good morning!

examples.trans: Good morning, everyone!
The weather is very nice today.

meanings.note: Electrical cord or wire.

examples.trans: The cord is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cables desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the cords from the door.

meanings.note: Plural los cafés (two coffees = dos cafés).

examples.trans: The coffee is here.

examples.text: Vemos los cafés desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the coffees from the door.

meanings.note: Describes hot drinks, food, or water.

examples.trans: It is a hot piece.

examples.text: Aquí tiene, señora: té caliente de menta con miel.
examples.trans: Here you are, madam: hot mint tea with honey.

meanings.note: Feminine noun: la calle.

examples.trans: The street is here.

examples.text: Vemos las calles desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the streets from the door.

meanings.note: En casa = at home (without article).

examples.trans: The house is here.

examples.text: Vemos las casas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the houses from the door.

meanings.note: Can take el or la, alongside dedicated feminine clienta.

examples.trans: The guest is here.

examples.text: Vemos los clientes desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the guests from the door.

meanings.note: Both the kitchen room and the stove/cuisine.

examples.trans: The kitchen is here.

examples.text: Vemos las cocinas desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the kitchens from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -er verb.

examples.text: Comemos juntos a las dos de la tarde.
examples.trans: We have lunch together at two in the afternoon.

examples.text: Comí un trozo de bizcocho de limón.
examples.trans: I ate a piece of lemon sponge cake.

meanings.note: Combines with mí/ti to form conmigo ('with me') and contigo ('with you').

examples.trans: I take coffee with hot milk.
Speak calmly, please.

meanings.note: Special fused form of con + mí.

examples.text: Ven conmigo al patio un minuto.
examples.trans: Come out to the courtyard with me for a minute.
Do you want to have breakfast with me?

meanings.note: Invariable cardinal number.

examples.trans: We have four tables inside.

examples.text: La habitación cuatro da al patio.
examples.trans: Room four looks out onto the courtyard.

meanings.note: Links possession, origin, material (de madera), and contents (taza de té).

examples.text: Es una mesa redonda de madera.
examples.trans: It is a round wooden table.

examples.text: Vengo de la estación de tren.
examples.trans: I am coming from the train station.

meanings.note: Dejar de + infinitive means 'to stop doing something'.

examples.text: Dejo las llaves en el mostrador.
examples.trans: I leave the keys on the counter.
Let me help you with that box.

meanings.note: Mandatory contraction of preposition de + masculine article el.

examples.text: El bizcocho acaba de salir del horno.
examples.trans: The cake just came out of the oven.
I am a neighbour from the quarter.

meanings.note: Los dos / las dos means 'both'.

examples.text: Pongo dos tazas azules en la mesa.
examples.trans: I put two blue cups on the table.

examples.text: Compra las dos válvulas por favor.
examples.trans: Buy both valves, please.

meanings.note: Definite article; also appears before feminine nouns starting with stressed /a/ (el agua, el asa).

examples.trans: The courtyard has plenty of light.
Pass me the reservation book.

meanings.note: Desde entonces = since then.

examples.text: ¿Entonces nos vemos mañana a las ocho?
examples.trans: So shall we see each other tomorrow at eight?
Since then she works with us.

meanings.note: Buen equipo = good team.

examples.trans: The team is here.

examples.text: Vemos los equipos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the teams from the door.

meanings.note: Forms: ese, esa, esos, esas.

examples.trans: Pass me that blue notebook.

examples.text: Esa maleta pertenece a un cliente.
examples.trans: That suitcase belongs to a guest.

meanings.note: Pairs with locations (está en el patio) and temporary states (está caliente).

examples.trans: Breakfast is ready now.
Where are the brass keys?

meanings.note: Used alone as an enthusiastic 'Exactly!'.

examples.trans: It is an exact piece.

examples.text: ¡Exacto! Ya eres una más del equipo.
examples.trans: Exactly! You are already one of the team.

meanings.note: Grammatically singular feminine noun in Spanish: la gente es amable.

examples.text: La gente es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The people is very important here.
We talk about the people.

meanings.note: Gracias por + noun/infinitive expresses 'thank you for...'.

examples.trans: Thank you very much for your help!
Thank you for coming today.

meanings.note: ¡Mucho gusto! = Pleased to meet you!; estar a gusto = to feel comfortable.

examples.text: El gusto es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The pleasure is very important here.
We talk about the pleasure.

meanings.note: Impersonal present form hay means 'there is / there are'; haber que + infinitive = must / need to.

examples.text: Hay pan caliente en la cocina.
examples.trans: There is warm bread in the kitchen.
We have already prepared the rooms.

meanings.note: Plural habitaciones.

examples.trans: The room is here.

examples.text: Vemos las habitaciones desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the rooms from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.text: Hablo con mi familia cada domingo.
examples.trans: I speak with my family every Sunday.

examples.text: Hablamos largo rato bajo el árbol.
examples.trans: We talked for a long while under the tree.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta luego! = See you later!; ¡Hasta mañana! = See you tomorrow!

examples.trans: Walk straight ahead as far as the bridge.
We are staying until Friday.

meanings.note: Irregular past participle of hacer (recién hecho = freshly made).

examples.trans: It is a made piece.

examples.text: ¡Son bollos recién hechos! Toma uno, todavía está caliente.
examples.trans: They are freshly baked rolls! Take one, it is still warm.

meanings.note: Universal friendly greeting at any hour of the day.

examples.trans: Hello, come in and sit down!
Hi, how are you doing today?

meanings.note: Definite feminine singular article before nouns; direct-object feminine pronoun before/attached to verbs.

examples.text: La puerta del patio es azul.
examples.trans: The courtyard door is blue.
The room has plenty of light.

meanings.note: Los viernes means 'every Friday / on Fridays'.

examples.trans: The neighbours come for breakfast.

examples.text: Daba clases de piano los viernes.
examples.trans: She taught piano lessons on Fridays.

meanings.note: Agrees before nouns (mucha agua, muchos años); invariable after verbs (llueve mucho).

examples.trans: Today we have a lot of work.
Thank you very much for the coffee.

meanings.note: Accented más means 'more / most'; de más = extra.

examples.trans: Would you like a little more tea?
It is the quietest room.

meanings.note: Requires no before the verb when nadie follows (no hay nadie).

examples.text: Todavía no hay nadie en el patio.
examples.trans: There is nobody in the courtyard yet.
Nobody knows this building better.

meanings.note: Placed directly before the verb (or object pronouns) to negate a sentence.

examples.trans: Today it is not raining in Valencia.

examples.text: No se preocupe por la hora.
examples.trans: Do not worry about the time.

nos.gloss: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)

meanings.en: us; to us; each other (¡Nos vemos!)
meanings.note: First-person plural object/reflexive/reciprocal pronoun.

examples.trans: See you tomorrow morning!
The news makes us very glad.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender and number with the thing possessed (nuestro patio, nuestra posada).

examples.trans: Our guesthouse has eight rooms.
Our neighbours have coffee here.

oler.gloss: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)

meanings.en: to smell (oler a = to smell of/like)
meanings.note: Irregular boot stem hue- (huelo, hueles, huele, huelen).

examples.text: La cocina huele a canela caliente.
examples.trans: The kitchen smells like warm cinnamon.

examples.text: El jardín huele a flores frescas.
examples.trans: The garden smells of fresh flowers.

meanings.note: Plural los panes; pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread.

examples.text: El pan es muy importante aquí.
examples.trans: The bread is very important here.
We talk about the bread.

meanings.note: Marks destination, recipient (para ti), deadline, and minutes to the hour (cinco para las doce).

examples.text: Este paquete blanco es para mi hermano.
examples.trans: This white parcel is for my brother.

examples.text: Faltan diez minutos para las doce.
examples.trans: It is ten minutes to twelve.

meanings.note: One word without accent (distinct from ¿por qué? = why?).

examples.text: Abro la ventana porque hace calor.
examples.trans: I open the window because it is warm.
She smiles because it smells of cinnamon.

meanings.note: ¡Hasta pronto! = See you soon!

examples.trans: See you soon and safe travels!

examples.text: Esta mañana me desperté muy pronto.
examples.trans: This morning I woke up very early.

qué.gloss: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)

meanings.en: what?; which?; how / what a! (in exclamations)
meanings.note: Used in questions (¿qué hora es?) and exclamations (¡qué alivio!).

examples.trans: What time is it right now?
What a bright morning!

meanings.note: Pan recién hecho = freshly baked bread; recién salido del horno = fresh out of the oven.

examples.text: Tenemos pan recién hecho cada día.
examples.trans: We have freshly baked bread every day.
The juice is freshly squeezed.

meanings.note: Hacer ruido = make noise; hay ruido = it is noisy.

examples.trans: The noise is here.

examples.text: Vemos los ruidos desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the noises from the door.

meanings.note: Regular -ar verb.

examples.trans: I greet the baker every morning.

examples.text: Nos saludaron desde el otro balcón.
examples.trans: They waved hello to us from the other balcony.

ser.gloss: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)

meanings.en: to be (identity, origin, time, permanent trait)
meanings.note: Used for names, professions, ownership (es mía), materials (es de madera), and clock time.

examples.text: Soy arquitecta y vivo en Valencia.
examples.trans: I am an architect and live in Valencia.
That blue suitcase is mine.

siempre.gloss: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)

meanings.en: always (siempre que = whenever / as long as)
meanings.note: Opposite of nunca.

examples.trans: The courtyard is always quiet.

examples.text: Ven siempre que quieras tomar café.
examples.trans: Come whenever you want to have coffee.

solo.gloss: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)

meanings.en: only; just (also adj solo/sola = alone / single)
meanings.note: Unaccented in modern RAE spelling; café solo = black espresso.

examples.trans: I only need five more minutes.
Only a single room remains vacant.

meanings.note: Stem-changing verb (o -> ue: suena).

examples.text: El despertador suena a las seis y media.
examples.trans: The alarm clock rings at six thirty.

examples.text: El piano sonaba cálido bajo la lluvia.
examples.trans: The piano sounded warm in the rain.

meanings.note: Tocar el timbre = ring the bell.

examples.trans: The bell is here.

examples.text: Vemos los timbres desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the bells from the door.

tocar.gloss: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)

meanings.en: to touch; to ring (a bell); to play (an instrument)
meanings.note: Preterite 1st sg spells c -> qu: toqué.

examples.text: Alguien acaba de tocar el timbre.
examples.trans: Someone just rang the bell.

examples.text: De niño tocaba el piano los viernes.
examples.trans: As a boy he played the piano on Fridays.

meanings.note: Everyday word for 'still' or 'not yet'.

examples.trans: The coffee is still hot.
It is not twelve o'clock yet.

meanings.note: Todo el día = the whole day; todo el mundo = everyone; sobre todo = mostly.

examples.text: Todo está limpio y en su sitio.
examples.trans: Everything is clean and in its place.

examples.text: Camina todo recto por esta calle.
examples.trans: Walk straight ahead down this street.

meanings.note: ¡Toma! = Here you go!; tomar un café = have a coffee.

examples.trans: What would you like to have for breakfast?
Here you go, here is the flashlight.

meanings.note: Nos tuteamos = let's use informal 'tú' with each other.

examples.text: Aquí nos tuteamos desde el primer día.
examples.trans: Here we use informal 'you' from day one.
May we use first-name terms over coffee?

meanings.note: Accented subject pronoun (tú mismo = you yourself).

examples.text: Tú conoces muy bien el barrio.
examples.trans: You know the neighbourhood very well.
Try it yourself.

meanings.note: Forms: un (m sg), una (f sg), unos (m pl 'some/about'), unas (f pl).

examples.text: Quiero un café caliente, por favor.
examples.trans: I would like a hot coffee, please.

examples.text: Hay una mesa libre en el patio.
examples.trans: There is a free table in the courtyard.

meanings.note: Shortens to un before masculine singular nouns.

examples.text: Toma uno recién salido del horno.
examples.trans: Take one fresh out of the oven.
We count from one to eight.

meanings.note: Takes 3rd-person singular verbs (¿quiere usted...?).

examples.trans: What is your name?

examples.text: Pase usted por aquí, por favor.
examples.trans: Come this way, please.

meanings.note: Opposite of lleno (full).

examples.trans: It is an empty piece.

examples.text: Aunque la cuatro está vacía, el cable viejo suena dos veces.
examples.trans: Even when room four is empty, the old wire rings twice.

meanings.note: La verdad = honestly / the truth.

examples.trans: The truth is here.

examples.text: Vemos las verdades desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the truths from the door.

vez.gloss: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)

meanings.en: time / occasion (dos veces = twice; en vez de = instead of)
meanings.note: Plural las veces; a veces = sometimes; otra vez = again.

examples.trans: The time / occasion is here.

examples.text: Vemos las veces desde la puerta.
examples.trans: We see the time / occasions from the door.

meanings.note: Before a noun (un viejo amigo), means 'long-standing / dear old'.

examples.trans: It is an old piece.
The old sunny attic room... follow me, quickly!

meanings.note: Changes to e before words starting with /i/ sound (i- or hi-).

examples.text: Servimos café caliente y pan fresco.
examples.trans: We serve hot coffee and fresh bread.
It is quarter past seven.

meanings.note: ¡Ya está! = All done!; ya no = no longer.

examples.trans: Breakfast is already ready.
Coming right now with the keys!
